title: Couples progress note note from F7: every section written + planted facts recalled
hypothesis: The Couples progress note template produces a complete note that captures the session's key facts.

sections.title: Attendance and presentation
sections.html: Clients Sam and Alex attended the 60-minute couple session. Both partners presented as engaged, though affect became tense during discussion of recent conflicts.

sections.title: Each partner's perspective
sections.html:
Alex raised concerns regarding a recent financial disagreement, specifically noting that Sam purchased an item costing eight hundred dollars without prior discussion, which led Alex to feel excluded and that their opinion does not matter.

Sam acknowledged Alex's perspective, expressing surprise and clarifying that Sam had previously perceived Alex's response as purely anger about the money rather than underlying feelings of being left out.

sections.title: Relational patterns
sections.html: The couple demonstrated a recurring communication pattern wherein discussions regarding financial stressors quickly escalate into defensive exchanges. During the session, Alex was able to move beyond primary anger to express vulnerable attachment emotions (feeling left out), which prompted a more empathetic and receptive response from Sam.

sections.title: Interventions
sections.html:
• Encouraged pacing and slowing down the interaction during escalation
  • Guided Alex to express primary emotional experiences rather than focusing solely on partner behaviors
  • Facilitated identification of softer emotions beneath surface anger
  • Collaboratively established a clear financial communication rule

sections.title: Plan
sections.html:
• Implement the newly agreed-upon rule requiring discussion prior to any purchases exceeding two hundred dollars
  • Continue practicing weekly check-ins while applying affective tracking and vulnerability in communication
  • Focus next session on reviewing the outcome of the weekly check-ins and addressing ongoing financial and relational dynamics
